bindings.label: Initial gastroscopic examination revealed lesions in the gastric antrum
A 52-year-old male presented on July 10, 2019 with an unremarkable past medical history

The patient underwent laparoscopy-assisted distal gastrectomy and Billroth II gastrojejunostomy on July 23, 2019, followed by eight cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with SOX regimen (oxaliplatin + tegafur, gimeracil and oteracil potassium) and 25 doses of radiotherapy in May 2020
During treatment, the patient experienced grade II neutrophils, grade I nausea, grade I neurotoxicity, grade II diarrhea with weight loss, rash, pruritus, and grade II oral ulcer

Postoperative pathology confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (diffuse type) with serosal invasion, pancreatic invasion, vascular tumor thrombus, perineural invasion, duodenal involvement, and 8/51 positive lymph nodes (pT4bN3a)
Molecular testing showed HER2 2+ with HER2 amplification in approximately 10% of tumor cells and intact MMR protein expression
